handoff.purpose: Define data structures, AST helpers, and baseline checks for write lanes.

symbols.name: WriteAttempt
symbols.note: Dataclass holding rel, proposed, repo_root, original, creating; property is_python.

symbols.name: CheckPolicy
symbols.note: Dataclass with elision_markers, min_size_ratio, min_symbol_survival, min_symbols_to_judge, first_party_roots, max_named_imports.

symbols.name: toplevel_defs
symbols.note: Returns frozenset of top-level function/class names, or None if parse fails.

symbols.name: _module_path
symbols.note: Resolves dotted name to Path; checks direct .py file or __init__.py.

symbols.name: _exports
symbols.note: Returns (frozenset of names, opaque bool) from AST; detects star imports and __getattr__.

symbols.name: parses
symbols.note: Refuses if proposed Python file does not parse; skips if original was unparsable.

symbols.name: not_truncated
symbols.note: Refuses if proposed size < min_size_ratio * original size.

symbols.name: no_elision
symbols.note: Refuses if elision marker appears in proposed but not original.

symbols.name: not_substituted
symbols.note: Refuses if too few top-level definitions survive; Python-only.

symbols.name: unresolved_first_party_imports
symbols.note: Returns list of unresolved first-party imports (truncated).

claims.text: A check returns "" to pass and a human-readable reason to refuse; a check that RAISES is treated as a refusal, because a guard that cannot answer must not be read as consent.
claims.why: All implemented checks (parses, not_truncated, no_elision, not_substituted) return "" on pass and a string on refusal; they do not raise exceptions (parses catches exceptions and returns refusal string).

claims.text: Every function here was lifted, not written: each one is a guard that already existed in ``providers/deepseek.py`` and each carries the measurement that put it there.
claims.why: The chunk does not include providers/deepseek.py; cannot verify origin.

claims.text: Deviation from the shape sketched in docs/HANDOFF_2026-07-30_NIGHT.md, which proposed ``Check = (rel, original, proposed, repo_root, policy) -> str``: the first four arguments are bundled into :class:`WriteAttempt`.
claims.why: The chunk does not include docs/HANDOFF_2026-07-30_NIGHT.md; cannot verify deviation.

claims.text: ``original`` is the exact current text, or "" when ``creating``. Keeping the two facts separate rather than inferring "creating" from an empty original matters: a lane that truncates a real file to nothing must not be able to present that as a creation and skip the guards that only run on edits.
claims.why: WriteAttempt has both original (default "") and creating (default False) fields; checks like not_truncated and not_substituted check attempt.creating or attempt.original emptiness to gate behavior.

claims.text: A Python file that will not parse is not an improvement.
claims.why: parses function returns a refusal string if proposed content fails to parse (SyntaxError, ValueError, RecursionError).

claims.text: Runs on CREATED files too, which is where the hole was: an edit that stops parsing was caught by :func:`not_substituted` as a side effect, but a brand-new module that does not parse had nothing looking at it -- the imports check returns early on a parse failure, calling it "a different guard's business". This is that guard.
claims.why: parses does not gate on attempt.creating; it runs for all Python files. not_substituted returns early if attempt.creating is True. The imports check (unresolved_first_party_imports) is truncated but likely returns early on parse failure.

claims.text: The classic full-rewrite failure: the model returned part of the file.
claims.why: not_truncated checks if proposed size < min_size_ratio * original size, detecting truncation.

claims.text: Only NEW markers count. A file that already contained the phrase would otherwise become permanently unwritable by this lane.
claims.why: no_elision checks that marker is in attempt.proposed.lower() and NOT in attempt.original.lower().

claims.text: Why this "rewrite" looks like the WRONG FILE, or "" if it looks fine.
claims.why: not_substituted returns refusal string if survival ratio below min_symbol_survival, else "".

claims.text: MEASURED 2026-07-30, and the reason this exists. A change request naming two files is sent once per file; asked to rewrite ``daedalus/shift.py`` the model returned the contents of ``tests/test_shift.py``. The module was destroyed and the run reported ``status: done``. Three of five multi-file writes failed exactly this way.
claims.why: Measurement data is not present in this chunk; cannot verify.

claims.text: None of the other guards can see it. Truncation compares SIZE, and a substituted file is a perfectly normal size -- the test module was in fact larger than the module it replaced. Elision looks for a model admitting it omitted something, and nothing was omitted: a complete, valid, well-formed file arrived. It was simply the wrong one.
claims.why: Behavior of other guards (truncation, elision) is described but not verified against this chunk; claims about their limitations are assertions without code evidence.

claims.text: So this asks the only question that separates the two cases: does the result still contain the thing that was sent? An edit keeps most of a file's top-level names; a substitution keeps none of them.
claims.why: not_substituted compares top-level definitions (toplevel_defs) of original and proposed; survival ratio is computed.

claims.text: Deliberately Python-only. The check needs a parser to be meaningful, and a guess about other languages would either fire on ordinary edits or provide false assurance for files it cannot actually read.
claims.why: not_substituted returns early if not attempt.is_python or attempt.creating.

claims.text: First-party imports in ``content`` that name nothing in the tree.
claims.why: Function is truncated; cannot verify behavior.

claims.text: MEASURED 2026-07-30. Twenty agents wrote test modules against source files they were given, and three of seven imported things that do not exist: ``daedalus.linting`` (it is ``daedalus.gui.lint``), ``ShiftManager`` from ``daedalus.shift`` (the class is ``Shift``), and ``daedalus.wiki_vault`` (it is ``daedalus.wiki.vault``). All three are valid Python, so a syntax gate passes them, and all three reported ``status: done``.
claims.why: Measurement data not present; function body truncated.

claims.text: The check is STATIC on purpose. Importing the file to find out whether its imports resolve would execute module-level code from an untrusted lane.
claims.why: Function body truncated; cannot confirm static approach.
